body:

  reading (with Run F's first-screen word), and «Session folder trusted by viola» cannot land its write as relied —
  that fork is the founder's, for the morning.

- Floor NOT held after the spares → the chunk wraps with the cause as far as it was named, the row still unverified,
  and a fourth start asked of the founder.

  reaches every binary its case needs; ids within 16 characters; «holds» = those cases ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT

# Phase directive — «Trust-record row read live» (Epoch 4's head entry, viola-0.2.0)

**The founder is AWAY for the night.** Raise NO question dialog at any step. A fork that would be his is written to
`{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, its options in order, the recommendation marked), the step stops there
and says so; the overseer answers technical forks by relay at once, and what is truly his waits for the morning —
a boundary widening takes its most conservative option. The review at P5 is plain text, as always.

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `f862f193`, nothing wider: the relied `trust-record`
   row read on the real 2.1.325 CLI, each interactive run's first screen named, before any product write relies
   on it. Nothing of `viola run` or `revive` changes; no capability is claimed.
2. **Ground already measured — read it, do not re-derive it:** the second cancelled take-up's `p3-block.md` (run
   `2026-11-17T22-05-41Z-phase`, sealed: `rec.py runs`) and chunk `2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row`'s report
   and evidence. `S0` read `verify-exit: 1 · 7/23 · trust-record: fail`; the writer's record equals the rig's
   seed; outside a repository the CLI's lookup climbs every parent; verify's children receive the kept
   `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. The working hypothesis — ONE common cause, not trust, stops runs B–F under the rig short
   of the input box — is unmeasured, and this chunk exists to measure it.
3. **Think before the start is spent — at P3, from the code, no start:** rows 1–7 passed and row 8
   (`input-box-signature`) on failed, in about 40 s for the whole verify. List every way verify's interactive
   child under the rig DIFFERS from the rig's own wrapped start that DID reach the input box on 2.1.325 (R2, R3,
   R3D of chunk 2026-11-17-first-readings-on-the-standing-rig): the argv (a model flag, `--settings`, a plugin
   dir, any flag verify adds), the environment after verify's strip (what the floor removes that the rig's
   wrapped start keeps — the credentials' reach, `HOME`, `TERM`, the terminal size), the cwd, the pty's size and
   how soon the screen is read, the timings a 40 s whole run implies (did each child exit, or was it cut?). For
   each difference say what first-screen word it predicts. The plan orders its instruments so ONE start tells
   them apart: the first-screen word per run, AND whatever closed fact separates the top candidates (the child's
   exit before the read, the count of settled frames, the run's wall) — closed words and numbers only, no screen
   text, nothing of his config.
4. **What the chunk builds** (the carry's list): verify keeps one closed first-screen word per interactive run in
   the stamp's `measured` (`trust` · `imports` · `box` · `none`, and a word for a child that exited — never a
   guess), the rig's `V` arm prints the six run lines before teardown; the `V` arm on a git-initialised cwd (Run F
   stays in its fresh dir outside any repository); the `verify_window_` kill and the 52 s case, with the measured
   walls; the `--record` witness of where the record went.
5. **The live starts — the founder's cap for THIS chunk** (his dialog answer read 2026-11-17T23:06:58Z, on the
   carry): ONE base start + TWO spares, each one live `viola verify` on the 2.1.325 install by path under the
   rig's private config (7 `claude` starts by the product's count). A spare is spent only AFTER a named cause:
   the start before it read below the floor and the cause it showed was MENDED (a code change — so through a plan
   revision, see item 6), or a start was lost to its shape. No key into any dialog or box by the rig; the stop is
   the standing one, and `stop:` is printed beside `keys:` for each start. Each start is ledgered with the clock's
   time before it is made; a start refused for the token window is uncounted — stop and say so, no timer. A
   fourth start is not made: it is his.
6. **The predicate, and what follows it.** The live entry reads RED when any of the 21 rows the live home's
   2.1.325 stamp passes reads below `pass`; `trust-record` itself may read either word. On RED implement STOPS
   before the operator pass, having written what the start showed (the six words and the closed facts), and says
   which candidate of item 3 it selects. The mend is then a plan revision through the phase's door (the door is
   open: no pre-CI commit was made), the re-entry spends the next spare. Plan the gate entries so the fake-agent
   work is green and landed in the tree BEFORE the first live start, and the live start is the last thing before
   the operator pass.
7. **Both ends are planned.** Floor held and `trust-record: pass` → the row is verified on 2.1.325 and the wrap
   says so, lifting «unverified» where it stands. Floor held and `trust-record: fail` → the row's premise is
   false on this CLI: say in the plan what the chunk lands then (the reading, the first-screen word of Run F) and
   that «Session folder trusted by viola» cannot land its write as relied — that fork is the founder's, for the
   morning. Floor NOT held after the spares → the chunk wraps with the cause as far as it was named, the row still
   unverified, and a fourth start asked of him.
8. No mutation run. Name each control's `--timeout S` in the plan's prose AND fire it with that flag, on an entry
   whose build reaches every binary its case needs; ids within 16 characters; «holds» = those cases ran and
   FAILED with no TIMEOUT line; for each control say what the subject does when the guard is gone.
9. A change to the fake agent's screens or to verify's runs puts `cli_verify` in the gate block. A test that waits

   host before the card.
10. Size: if P3 finds this past one implement window, stop at P3's end with a block; otherwise go on through P4

11. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start.
12. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the

    in the union or its standing list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal,
    `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` / `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

data.head: ## P3 difference list (directive item 3) — verify's interactive child vs the rig's wrapped start that reached the box

body: Read from the code at `f862f193`, no start. Each difference with the first-screen word it predicts for Runs B–F:

1. **Terminal size** — verify's child is 80×24 (`run.rs:85`, `Size::DEFAULT`); the wrapped R3/R3D child took the
   rig's 210×45 through `viola run`'s outer pty. Predicts `none` (the box or footer not on the rows the signatures
   read) if the CLI draws a near-empty config's start screen differently at 80 columns. A live 2.1.325 verify under
   the user's own config passed at 80×24, so size ALONE is excluded; size × private config is not.

2. **The config's content** — the live home's passing verify read the user's own config; S0 and R3 read the rig's
   private config (`hasCompletedOnboarding` + one trust entry). R3 reached the box in it, so the private config

- (arch) A stamping verify over the fake agent with `--screens` writes `measured.first_screen` `a: trust`, `b`–`f`:
  `box`, and six `first_settle_ms` numbers below 8 500
  (`verify_first_screens_read_trust_then_box_on_the_fake`); without screens, all six `none` at 8 500 ms or more
  (`verify_window_without_screens_fails_every_interactive_row`); no row's word and no `run` field reads them
  (architecture `contract/ledger-stamps/measured`).

- (arch) The classifier maps each literal to its word, modal before box, and an ended child with no literal to
  `exited`, absent rows included (`first_screen_reads_each_literal_then_the_exit`); `exited` is proven at the unit tier
  only (no fake-agent mode exits at start without a key).

- (arch) The stamp merge writes both maps, `null` for a run that never started
  (`merge_stamp_writes_the_six_first_screens_and_their_settles`).

- (security) No screen text, frame, config value, path or key reaches the stamp or the rig's summary: closed words,
  whole numbers and row ids only (security `decision/verify-screen-read-against-literals`,
  `decision/live-session-screens-kept-local`).

- (tests) A `--record` verify writes its trust record only into the file its kept `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names, reads
  `trust-record: pass` from it, and leaves that file with no `viola-verify-` key and its sentinel value-equal
  (`verify_record_writes_its_trust_record_to_the_kept_config_dir_only`).

- (tests) The `verify_window_` class takes an 80 s kill in both profiles, its override still first in `mutants`
  (`mutants_verify_window_override_stands_before_the_harness_package_override`); the planted-hang pair and the
  no-screen case's wall under the moved kill are recorded in `evidence/kill-80s.txt`.
- (tests) The three controls `fs-trust`, `fs-record`, `rig-gitroot` hold (each named case failed, no TIMEOUT line).

- (tests) Every block entry before the live round is green: `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --unit`, `bash
  scripts/agent-run.sh run --integration`, `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --e2e` and the rest.

- (live) S0R runs once on 2.1.325 by path under the rig's private config, ledgered with the clock's time first,
  `keys: none`, `stop:` printed beside it, and its summary records the six words, six walls, `verify-exit`,
  `trust-record`, `pass-count` and `failing:` as read. The reading takes one of plan step 11's four ends, recorded as
  read and never as verification unless the floor held and `trust-record` read `pass` (test-plan
  `decision/live-failing-reading-not-verification`).

- (CI) The pushed HEAD's CI reads `verdict: green` (`ci.py conclusion --sha HEAD --wait 1800`) — reached only on a
  held floor.
- No capability is claimed: `matrix#v2-33` stays pooled (cry-ufpnw7gv).

- Rows: architecture `decision/screen-signatures-compiled`, `decision/verify-child-set`,
  `decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs`, `decision/trust-record-ledger-row`, `contract/ledger-stamps/measured`,
  `decision/vt100-readiness-gate`, `decision/poisoned-screen-model`; security
  `decision/input-box-readiness-from-literals`, `decision/verify-screen-read-against-literals`,
  `decision/live-session-screens-kept-local`, `decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty`,
  `decision/live-rig-isolated-child`, `decision/trust-record-closed-words`; test-plan
  `decision/verify-window-60s-kill`, `decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill`, `decision/standing-live-rig`,
  `decision/live-failing-reading-not-verification`, `decision/verify-under-test-owned-user-home`,
  `decision/no-verify-start-outside-test-home`, `decision/record-home-names-no-home`; obs-plan
  `decision/trust-record-write-uninstrumented`, `decision/no-telemetry-from-screen-content`,
  `decision/verify-lines-carry-no-content`.

- History: architecture 2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box (the box predicate and the additive `measured`
  precedent), 2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows (the footer trap behind S0's pattern), 2026-10-17-optional-plugin-install
  (a git-initialised cwd met the trust dialog: why the seed is keyed at the root); test-plan
  2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup and 2026-10-07-send-waits-out-the-paste-hint (a kill moves only for a floor by design,
  with the planted-hang pair).

- Research: `src/cmd/verify/typed/{run,runs,pty,turns}.rs`, `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`,
  `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/{screen,ledger}.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/{mod,isolate,ledger}.rs`,
  `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`,
  `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs`, `.config/nextest.toml`, `tests/contract_lints.rs`, `tests/support/verify.rs`; S0's round
  record `chunks/2026-11-17-trust-record-ledger-row/evidence/round-203938Z.txt`.
- External: inputs#I1 (the overseer's phase directive).

- Spawning `git init` from the rig — rejected: it adds a process crossing to the rig's isolated start (security
  `decision/live-rig-isolated-child`), a widening no founder answer covers; git's own minimal layout written as files is
  a repository by git's definition and spawns nothing (leaned per that row and inputs#I1's «a boundary widening takes
  its most conservative option»).
- A new verify wait, key or paste to read a screen — never: every reading rides a settle the run already makes.
- A first-screen word stamped as a row value, or read by `run` — never: `measured` only.
- Raising the `verify_window_` kill without the planted-hang pair — never (testing.md 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05).

- Asserting the real `~/.claude.json` untouched — never: the host's own sessions rewrite it (host-linux.md
  2026-11-17).
- A spare spent on a red whose cause was not named and mended — never (cry-r6ctt6nh); a fourth start — the founder's.
- Re-stamping the live home, or touching `viola run` / `revive` — not this chunk's.

- The live summary's line numbers in the S0R `note` atoms are read at P4 at `f862f193`
  (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`); implement re-reads them after step 6 moves the file.

- The 52 s wall: 52.2–52.3 s over three implement runs (the previous report's Watches line); the 60 s kill's sizing
  basis 42.9–43.7 s (tests history 2026-10-20-epoch-5-cleanup). Predicted under the moved kill: the case still near
  52 s — record what the re-run measures.

  `2026-11-17T22-05-41Z-phase` §(c)), read from the live home's stamp there.

  settle walls (`first_screen`, `first_settle_ms`).
- Expected amendments (wrap): test-plan `decision/verify-window-60s-kill` — the class kill is 80 s, with the walls.

# P5 review — «Trust-record row read live», plan of 2026-11-18 (card 1)

Technical, the overseer's; no founder fork in it. The plan stands but for one gap: by your own expectation the
first start reads RED with `none` on runs B–F — and `none` does not NAME a cause. A start that returns «an
unrecognised screen, five times» spends a third of the founder's cap and mends nothing. Revise on these points,
then put the card again.

1. **The directive's item 3 — where is it?** The card says what the 40 s implies (four full 8.5 s settles) and
   nothing of the list: every way verify's interactive child under the rig DIFFERS from the rig's own wrapped
   start that reached the input box on 2.1.325 (R2, R3, R3D) — the argv verify gives the child, the environment
   after verify's strip against what the rig's wrapped start keeps, the cwd, the pty's size, when the screen is
   read. Put that table in the plan (the difference · where in the code · the first screen it predicts), from the
   code, no start. If one difference is a likely cause on its face — a variable the strip removes that the
   credentials or the config need, an argument the wrapped start never passes — say so, and say whether it can be
   tested on the fake agent or by a unit case BEFORE a start is spent.
2. **Make `none` speak.** Beside each run's word and settle time, verify keeps closed FACTS it already holds at
   that settle, numbers and closed words only, no screen text, nothing of his config:
   - the bytes the child's terminal produced before the settle (0 says the child drew nothing);
   - whether the child was alive at the read, and its exit status if it had exited;
   - the count of non-empty rows of the settled screen, and whether the screen changed at all after the first
     frame (a static unknown screen against one still drawing);
   - for each existing signature family, whether ANY of its literals matched (`modal-any`, `box-any`), so «no
     signature» is told from «a signature of another family».
   Choose the set so that the candidates of point 1 predict DIFFERENT rows of facts; say which fact separates
   which candidates, and drop a fact that separates none. The rig's `V` arm prints them per run.
3. **What a red start then does.** With the facts printed, the outcome names one candidate of the table or says
   «none of the listed» with the facts as read; the plan says, for each candidate, the mend it implies and whether
   that mend is this chunk's (a rig or verify change inside the scope) or the founder's (anything that would keep
   screen text, widen what verify reads or writes, or change the product's start). No spare is spent on an
   unnamed cause.
4. Accepted as written: the six words and times in the stamp's `measured`; the git root made by writing git's own
   minimal files (say what the CLI needs to see to treat it as a root — measured from the bundle, not assumed —
   and what the start reads if it does not); the kill at 80 s with its planted-hang check; the `--record` witness;
   the ledger counting `-3`; the labels `S0R` · `S0R-2` · `S0R-3`; the 21-row floor as must-be-absent from the
   failing-rows line (say what the entry reads if that line itself is missing — it must be RED, never green by
   absence).

body:
Read from the code at `f862f193` and the installed 2.1.325 bundle, no start. Three references reached the input box on
2.1.325: the rig's wrapped starts R3 / R3D (`viola run` under the same private config, `--model haiku`, the seeded
cwd itself; chunk 2026-11-17-first-readings-on-the-standing-rig, evidence/live-starts.md) and the live home's own
verify (its 2.1.325 stamp passes 21 rows: verify's children at 80×24 under the user's own config, from the user's
trusted repository). S0 differs from each as follows:
| # | Difference | Where in the code | vs R3/R3D | vs the live-home verify | First screen it predicts on B–F |

| D1 | argv | verify: program args + `--model haiku` (`src/cmd/verify/typed.rs:77-78`), then `--plugin-dir <its capture plugin>` (B, C, D, E; `runs.rs:96-101`, `:113-114`, `:160-161`, `:193-194`), C adds `--settings <dialog settings>`, D `--permission-mode plan --settings <plans>`, A and F no plugin; run: `--plugin-dir <pinned viola plugin>` first, then `--model haiku` (`src/run/mod.rs:137-148`, `viola-live-rig.rs:197-199`) | same model; another plugin; flag order differs | same argv | a plugin-load prompt verify's capture plugins meet in a fresh config: an unknown modal, `none` |

| D2 | environment after the strip | both through the one `viola_agent_claude::plan_strip` over the vhome's `claude_env_keep` (`src/cmd/verify.rs:181`; run's persistent names, `src/run/env.rs:17`) over the rig's `child_env` (`HOME USER LOGNAME SHELL PATH LANG XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `TERM=xterm-256color`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, the rig marker; `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs:23-31`, `:134-153`); run adds `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR`, `VIOLA_BIN` (`src/run/mod.rs:137-140`) | equal but the three `VIOLA_*` names | the user's whole shell environment vs the rig's closed list | none on its face: no name the strip removes is one the credentials or the config need (the print probe passed rows 01–07 under the same env and config) |

| D3 | config | `<scratch>/config/.claude.json` = `{"hasCompletedOnboarding":true,"projects":{<cwd>:{"hasTrustDialogAccepted":true}}}` and the copied credentials (`isolate.rs:252-263`) | same config | the user's own, long-used config | a first-run notice of a near-empty config: an unknown screen, `none` |

| D4 | cwd | B–E in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid><suffix>` (`runs.rs:284-290`), trusted through the ancestor record; A, F fresh `viola-verify-` OS-temp dirs | R3 stood in the seeded cwd itself (exact key) | the user's trusted repository | `trust` on B–E if the ancestor walk does not reach (the bundle's `SS` walk says it does) |

| D5 | pty size | verify's children 80×24 (`run.rs:85`, `Size::DEFAULT`) | R3's child took the rig's 210×45 (`rig/screen.rs:11-12`) through `viola run` | the same 80×24 | with D3: a box drawn that the predicate does not accept at 80 columns, `none` with a box literal standing |

| D6 | when the screen is read | verify settles from the spawn: 300 ms quiet with a literal, else at 8.5 s (`pty.rs:145-163`) | R3 waited for its `session-start` event, then `send`'s gate (8.5 s more) — no bound on the start's own time | the same settle | a start slower than 8.5 s in a fresh config: `none`, bytes still arriving near the read |

| D7 | a sibling killed before | Run A is killed at its trust modal before B starts (`runs.rs:36-37`, `end_by_kill`) | no killed sibling before R3 | the same kill | a state a killed start leaves in a fresh config blocking the next start: `none`, nothing drawn |

**A cause likely on its face:** none of the seven is decisive from the code alone. D2 (the environment) is excluded as
a cause: verify and run apply the one strip to the one environment, and the print probe passed under it. D5 alone is
excluded by the live home's verify (80×24, passing); D3 alone by R3 (the private config, passing); what stands is a
combination unique to S0 — D3 with D1, D5, D6 or D7, or D4. **Testable before a start:** none of the candidate CAUSES
can be tested on the fake agent (it draws what it is told, never what 2.1.325 draws in a fresh config) or by a unit case;
what IS tested before the start is that each fact reads its known value on the fake (step 5), so the start's reading is
the only new measurement.

**The git root (inputs#I2 point 4), measured from the 2.1.325 bundle, not assumed:** the CLI's `jt` (logged as
`find_git_root`) walks from the cwd up and stops at the first folder where `xvn(<folder>/.git)` holds: `lstat` reads a
directory or a file, or a symbolic link that resolves to a directory or file outside itself; its async twin `t4o`
takes a directory or file and refuses a link. No content of `.git` is read to decide the root. So a real `.git`
directory — the layout step 6 writes — is a root to both. If the CLI did NOT read it as a root, B–E's trust reading is
unchanged: outside a repository the `SS` walk climbs every parent and meets the seeded cwd's record (the measured
ground, inputs of chunk 2026-11-17-session-folder-trusted-by-viola-2's P3 block). The root moves only what the CLI keys
on it (the imports approval, project-local state), not the trust reading.

1. **The closed first-screen word and its facts — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs`.**
   - A closed word type `FirstScreen` (`trust` · `imports` · `box` · `none` · `exited`, `as_str` the kebab word) and
     one pure classifier over a settled reading: rows holding `SIGNATURES.modals[0]` → `trust`; else holding
     `SIGNATURES.modals[1]` → `imports`; else `SIGNATURES.input_box_up(rows)` → `box`; else `exited` when the child had
     ended by the read, else `none`. Absent rows (a poisoned screen, `Screen::rows` `None`) take the last two arms. The
     order is modal before box (security `decision/input-box-readiness-from-literals`: «never while a modal literal
     stands»).
   - One pure fact reader over the same rows: `rows` the count of non-empty rows (`null` for absent rows) and
     `box_any`, whether ANY input-box-family literal stands on any row — a footer literal (`holds_footer`), a rule row
     (`is_box_rule`) or a row opening `box_prompt` — so «a box the predicate did not accept» is told from «no box at
     all». No modal-family fact is kept: a modal literal already makes the word `trust` or `imports`, so on a `none`
     word a modal fact would always read false and separate nothing (inputs#I2 point 2, «drop a fact that separates
     none»).
   - An inline rstest table, `first_screen_reads_each_literal_then_the_exit`, one case a word plus trust-over-box and
     the two absent-rows cases, and `first_screen_facts_count_rows_and_any_box_literal` (a footer alone, a rule alone,
     a prompt row alone, none, absent rows) (keeps tests S1, S4).

2. **The stamp keeps the readings — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`.** `TypedRun` gains the six readings
   (one per run A–F, each `None` or: the word, `settle_ms`, `bytes`, `alive`, `exit`, `rows`, `box_any`,
   `last_byte_ms`). `merge_stamp` writes three maps beside `trust_probe` in the version's `measured`:
   `first_screen` `{"a": word|null, …}`, `first_settle_ms` `{"a": ms|null, …}` and `first_facts`
   `{"a": {"bytes":n,"alive":bool,"exit":n|null,"rows":n|null,"box_any":bool,"last_byte_ms":n|null}|null, …}`. Its
   signature does not change (callers: `src/cmd/verify.rs:272`, the version-gate and ledger tests — research §Graph
   impact). No row's word reads them; `run` reads no field of `measured` (architecture `contract/ledger-stamps/measured`:
   «additions need no v bump, and run reads no field of it»). The full literal `clean_typed()` in
   `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases.rs:113` gains the fields; the 28 spread literals need nothing
   (research §Sweeps). `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger/test_cases_stamps.rs` gains
   `merge_stamp_writes_the_six_first_screens_their_settles_and_facts` (every word, a `null` run, an exited run's exit
   status) (keeps tests S4).

3. **A run's first reading — `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs`.** `Run` gains one reading over a settle it already made,
   from state it already holds: the word and facts of step 1 from the settled rows; `alive` = the pump not finished at
   that instant (`self.pump.is_finished()`); `bytes` = the `Feed`'s `total`; `settle_ms` = `settled.at − spawned_at`;
   `last_byte_ms` = the `Feed`'s `last_fed − spawned_at`, `null` when nothing was fed. `exit` is filled once the run
   ends, from the status its `finish` already joins (`run.rs:210-227`), and only when the child was not alive at the
   read (a kill's status is never recorded as the start's exit). A settle that returns `None` (the stop) gives no
   reading. `input_box_settles` keeps its bool and also hands back the reading of the same settle.

4. **Each run records its reading — `src/cmd/verify/typed/runs.rs`.** Run A: its `modal` settle. Run B: its `ready`
   settle. Runs C and D: the settle `input_box_settles` already makes. Run E: the settle after its SessionStart
   capture; when no SessionStart is captured by its deadline, the reading is taken from the rows, the feed and the pump
   state at that instant, with no added wait. Run F: its `trust_frame` settle. A run that never spawns — Run E with no
   resume target, Run F with no record written — leaves its reading `None` (`null`). No run waits longer, pastes
   anything more, or types a key. `src/cmd/verify/typed.rs`'s module comment names the readings.

5. **The fake-agent cases — each fact read at a known value before the start — `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs` and
   `tests/cli_verify.rs`.**
   - `verify_first_screens_read_trust_then_box_on_the_fake` (`tests/cli_verify/runs.rs`): a stamping verify over the
     recorded set with `--screens`; `first_screen` reads `a: trust`, `b`–`f`: `box`; each `first_settle_ms` below
     8 500; each `first_facts` reads `bytes` above 0, `alive` true, `exit` null, `rows` above 0, `box_any` true for
     `b`–`f` (the oracle literals copied from the first run's output, testing.md 2026-10-16) (keeps tests S1–S4, S6).
   - `verify_window_without_screens_fails_every_interactive_row` keeps its assertions and adds: `first_screen` `a`–`f`
     all `none`, each `first_settle_ms` at least 8 500, `alive` true, `box_any` false, `rows` 0 — the fake drawing
     nothing without `--screens`, which is the known value of the D7 row («nothing drawn») on the fake; `bytes` and
     `last_byte_ms` are asserted as read on the first run (the fake's no-screen output copied as its oracle, testing.md
     2026-10-16). Its doc comment names the moved kill (step 7).
   - `verify_record_writes_its_trust_record_to_the_kept_config_dir_only` (`tests/cli_verify.rs`): a `--record`
     verify (the shared record-home helper, testing.md 2026-11-15: no component named `home`) whose kept
     `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` names the test-owned user home with one sentinel project entry: `trust-record` reads `pass`
     (the fake agent was told only that file), and after the run that file holds no `viola-verify-` key and the
     sentinel value-equal. It asserts nothing of the real `~/.claude.json` (cry-nuv2dovv).
   - `exited` and a non-null `exit` are proven at the unit tier only (steps 1, 2): no fake-agent mode exits at start
     without a key.
   - Every new verify start runs under a test-owned home (the census `every_test_verify_runs_under_a_test_home`) and
     passes `--transcript` beside `--framing` (tests history 2026-11-16-local-command-delivery).

6. **The V arm — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` and `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`.**
   - `Scratch` gains one step, run for the `V` arm only before `seed_config`: the cwd made a git root by git's own
     minimal layout written as files — a real `.git/` directory holding `HEAD` (`ref: refs/heads/main`) and empty
     `objects/` and `refs/` — no `git` process spawned (§Constraints). What the CLI needs of it is `.git` as a directory
     (the bundle's `jt`/`xvn`, §Difference table). The seed's key is the cwd's canonical spelling (`fs::canonicalize`).
     A layout that cannot be written refuses the start `seed`. The summary gains `git-root: <word>` read from the disk
     after the step, not from the step's result: `written` when `<cwd>/.git` is a directory holding a regular `HEAD`,
     else `absent`.
   - `arm_v`, after verify's exit and before the teardown, reads the vhome stamp's version entry (`stamp_reading`,
     `rig/mod.rs:777`) and puts, per run `x` of `a`–`f`: `screen-x: <word>`, `settle-x: <ms>` and
     `facts-x: bytes=<n> alive=<yes|no> exit=<n|null> rows=<n|null> box=<yes|no> last=<ms|null>` — a value that is not
     a code word or a whole number reads `unread`, a run `null` reads `null`. It puts `rows: <n>`, the number of row
     ids the version entry holds, and `failing: <ids>`, the ids whose value is not `pass`, comma-joined in the stamp's
     order, or `failing: none`; when the stamp or its version entry cannot be read, `failing: unread` and `rows:
     unread`. Closed words, row ids and numbers only; no screen text, frame or config value is printed (security
     `decision/live-session-screens-kept-local`).
   - `Arm::of_label` takes `S0R` (the base start S0′, spelled here per cry-r6ctt6nh), `S0R-2` and `S0R-3` (the two
     spares) as `V`.
   - `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`: `rig_rehearsal_v_reads_the_trust_record_row_and_no_record_left`
     asserts `git-root: written`, `screen-a: trust`, `screen-b` … `screen-f: box`, every `settle-*` a number, every
     `facts-*` line present with `alive=yes`, `rows: 23` and `failing: none`, beside what it asserts today; a
     rig unit case `stamp_reading_reads_unread_for_an_absent_version` holds that a stamp with no entry for the version
     prints `failing: unread` (keeps arch S1, S2; tests S2, S3).

10. **The live start S0R — the round entries of the block.** Read the 2.1.325 install by path, census the rig, build
    `viola` and read its hash right before the start (verification-harness.md 2026-10-20), ledger and fire `S0R`,
    census again. `keys: none` (no key by the rig into any dialog or box; verify pastes only its own ratified literals);
    `stop:` is printed beside `keys:` (the standing stop: Ctrl-C into its own pty or a no-key group kill, which needs
    no word, security `decision/live-round-rig-keys-own-pty`). A start the rig refuses for the token window
    (`refused: token-window`) is uncounted: implement stops and says so, and sets no timer.

11. **Reading the start: the candidate it names, the mend, and whose mend it is (inputs#I2 point 3).** Implement
    records the summary whole in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-18-trust-record-row-read-live/evidence/live-starts.md`.
    - **The floor.** The floor is broken when any of the 21 floor rows appears on `failing:`, and the live entry reads
      RED then. It reads RED too when the line is missing (`contains failing:`), reads `failing: unread`
      (`lacks failing: unread`), or the version entry holds fewer than the 23 relied rows (`contains rows: 23`): a
      floor row absent from the stamp can never read green by its absence (inputs#I2 point 4).
    - **A red names its cause before anything else.** Implement STOPS before the operator pass, writes the six words,
      walls and fact rows, `verify-exit`, `pass-count`, `rows:` and `failing:`, and matches B–F's facts against this
      table, naming ONE candidate, or «none of the listed» with the facts as read:

      | Candidate (difference) | word on B–F | bytes | alive / exit | rows | box_any | last_byte_ms | The mend it implies | Whose |
      |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
      | K1 a box the predicate does not accept at 80×24 in the fresh config (D3+D5) | `none` | > 0 | yes / null | > 0 | yes | well before 8 500 | the compiled box predicate, or verify's fixed 80×24 — the one predicate `run`'s pre-send gate shares (security `decision/input-box-readiness-from-literals`), and the ratified child set's size (`decision/verify-child-set`) | the founder's |
      | K2 the ancestor record not honoured (D4) | `trust` on B–E, `box` on F | > 0 | yes / null | > 0 | no | early | verify writing a record per run dir, a widening of what verify writes | the founder's |
      | K3 an unknown modal or first-run notice — a plugin-load prompt (D1) or a fresh-config notice (D3) | `none` | > 0 | yes / null | > 0 | no | well before 8 500 | a new compiled literal (which moves `run`'s gate too), or naming the screen, which needs its text | the founder's |
      | K4 nothing drawn: a start blocked, as by a state a killed sibling leaves in a fresh config (D7) | `none` | 0, or rows 0 | yes / null | 0 | no | null or early | how verify ends Run A (a key into its dialog is never allowed) or a wait in verify for the leftover; or the rig's own scratch setup when the leftover is the rig's | the founder's, but this chunk's when the leftover lies in the rig's setup |
      | K5 a start slower than 8.5 s in the fresh config (D6) | `none` | > 0 | yes / null | any | any | at or after about 8 000 | a longer first-screen bound in verify's own runs, inside verify, not the gate `run` shares | this chunk's |
      | K6 the child exited at start (D1, D2) | `exited` | any | no / its code | any | any | any | by the exit code: a name the rig's closed env list lacks is the rig's (`isolate.rs:23-31`); an argument or strip of verify's is the child set's | this chunk's for the rig's env; else the founder's |
      | K7 a poisoned screen at 80×24 | `none` | > 0 | yes / null | null | no | any | verify's feed (a poisoned model unpoisons only at a size change, `decision/poisoned-screen-model`) | this chunk's |

    - **What follows the name.** A mend that is this chunk's goes through a plan revision through the phase's door (no
      pre-CI commit made), and its re-entry spends `S0R-2`; a red after it, with its cause named and mended by a further
      revision, spends `S0R-3`. A mend that is the founder's is written to the run's `founder-forks.md` (the question,
      its options, the recommendation marked) and the chunk spends no spare on it: it wraps with the cause named and
      the row unverified. «None of the listed» spends no spare: the facts go to the founder with the reading. A start
      lost to its shape (the rig's own refusal past the ledger line, a census left over) spends the next spare with no
      mend. No spare is ever spent on an unnamed cause; a fourth start is the founder's.
    - **Floor held, `trust-record: pass`** — the row is verified on 2.1.325 in the rig's private home; the wrap says so
      and lifts «unverified» where it stands. The live home is not re-stamped («The 2.1.325 recorded fixture set»,
      `cry-bb5cy7aq`).
    - **Floor held, `trust-record: fail`** — the row's premise is false on this CLI. The chunk lands the instruments
      and the reading, Run F's word and facts named, and «Session folder trusted by viola» cannot land its write as
      relied: that fork is the founder's, for the morning (`founder-forks.md`).
    - **Floor not held after the spares** — the chunk wraps with the cause as far as it was named, the row unverified,
      and a fourth start asked of the founder.
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` — the closed first-screen word, its classifier and its row facts (step 1)
- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `TypedRun`'s six readings; `merge_stamp`'s three `measured` maps (step 2)
- `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs` — a run's reading over its settle, and its exit at the end (step 3)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — the reading lines, `rows:`, `failing:`, `git-root:` and the `S0R` labels (step 6)

The block runs the formatter and linter, the agent crate's unit suite (the classifier, the facts, the stamp merge), the
root bin's unit layer, the changed integration binaries by name (`cli_verify` is in it: verify's runs change,
verification-harness.md 2026-11-17; `contract_ledger_probes` and `cli_version_gate` read the stamps; `contract_lints`
pins the moved override's order; `rig_rehearsal` is the V arm's rehearsal), then the whole integration and E2E layers
(every stamped binary and the harness boot copy the new `measured`), then the live round for S0R and the operator
pass. The release check is not run: no test-only feature, binary or fake-agent code changes (the rig and its ledger

harness boot, so the operator pass boots one session `screen-smoke`, reads its status and cleans it up (boot never

  (step 6), so with the guard gone the V arm's cwd holds no `.git`, the word reads `absent` and the case's

body:
# Live starts — 2026-11-18-trust-record-row-read-live

Cap (the founder's R6): 1 base start S0R + 2 spares (S0R-2, S0R-3), each one live `viola verify` on the 2.1.325
install by path; a spare only after a named cause whose mend is this chunk, landed through a plan revision.

Spent: **1 of 3** (S0R). Spares spent: **0**.

## S0R — RED

- Ledgered by the rig before the start: `2026-11-18T01:22:58Z` (`live-starts.ndjson`, its `start` line); summary
  written `2026-11-18T01:23:36Z`. The round fired at `2026-11-18T01:22:52Z` (`round-012252Z.txt`).
- Install read by path first (entry 8 green, `2.1.325 (Claude Code)`); `mise ls claude` read `2.1.326` as `latest`
  at 01:22:47Z — not used (the cap names 2.1.325).
- Build hash read right before the start (entry 10): `b92c4721eb8d16dc`, equal to the summary's `viola-build`.
- Census before (entry 9): `census: 0`; the rig's own census after: `census: 0` (by hand at 01:24:24Z — the round
  stopped before entry 12); `gate.py census` read 9 host `claude` sessions, all on the `latest` install, none
  started by this run.

The summary, whole (gate log `$TMPDIR/andromeda-gate/2026-11-18-trust-record-row-read-live/implement-2026-11-18T01-02-09Z/11.log`):

```

viola-build: b92c4721eb8d16dc

```

## The floor

Broken: 14 of the 21 floor rows read below `pass` (`input-box-signature` through `local-command-compact`, every
row from the input-box signature on); rows 01–07 pass, as in S0. `local-command-echo` and `trust-record` (not floor)
read `fail`. `rows: 23` and `failing:` stood, so the reading is whole, not a missing line.

## The candidate (plan step 11)

Runs B, C, D and F read alike: `none` · bytes 1167–1319 · alive, no exit · rows 9–10 · `box_any` yes ·
last byte 322–651 ms, all far before 8 500 (the screen was quiet ~8 s before the read). Run E started no child (no
SessionStart captured on Run B, so no resume target — `resume-session` fails for that, not for its own start).

Against the table, every column matches **K1 — a box the predicate does not accept at 80×24 in the fresh config
(D3+D5)**: `none`, > 0, yes / null, > 0, yes, well before 8 500. Mend: the compiled box predicate (the one `run`'s
pre-send gate shares) or verify's fixed 80×24 — **the founder's**.

**Caveat, as measured, not fitted:** Run A's trust screen reads `box_any` yes too (`facts-a … box=yes`) — the
2.1.325 trust form draws a row the box family accepts (a rule of at least 40 `─`, or a row opening `❯`). So
`box_any` yes does not by itself show an input box drawn: on B–F it says only that a rule row or a `❯`-led row
stood, with no footer literal and no rule directly above a `❯`-led row (else `input_box_up` would have read `box`,
no modal standing). K3 (an unknown first-run notice drawing such a row) is therefore not excluded by this start;
the table's K3 row assumed `box_any` no. K1 and K3 both have the founder's mend, so the disposition is the same.

What the reading rules out: K2 (no `trust` on B–E: the ancestor record / git-root key held), K4 (bytes and rows
> 0: something drawn), K5 (last byte 322–651 ms, not near 8 000), K6 (alive, no exit), K7 (rows not null).

## Disposition

The mend is the founder's → no spare spent (R6: a spare only after a named cause whose mend is this chunk). The fork
is written to the run's `founder-forks.md` (`.andromeda/runs/2026-11-18T01-02-09Z-implement/founder-forks.md`).
Implement stopped before the operator pass. The row stays unverified on 2.1.325; nothing here is verification
(test-plan `decision/live-failing-reading-not-verification`).

- pty: 80×24, `viola_pty::Size::DEFAULT`, the constant verify's children take (`run.rs:85`).

- cwd and config: the `V` arm's own seed — the git root written as files, the trust record at the root's canonical
  key, the six markers (`seed_used_markers` at the version read from the program by path) — and the cwd the seeded
  root itself, a folder the seed trusts.
- Unwrapped: nothing of viola stands between the child and the screen.

- What is left of verify's shape, not reproduced and named: the timing (verify reads at most 8.5 s from the spawn;
  this start settles as `first_frame` does, up to its `--settle 60`), the sequence (verify's print probe, then Run A
  killed at its trust dialog, before B), and the cwd (B in a subfolder of the root, F in a temp dir outside any
  repository; B and F read alike, so the cwd is already set aside).

**What Revision 2 adds:** steps 17–20 below. Implement re-enters at **step 17**: steps 1–16 stand as built, the tree
carrying them uncommitted. Steps 10, 11 and 16's live entries are spent and are not in the block; the block's live
entry is the naming start `S0C`.

16. **The second start `S0R-2` — the live round, re-fired (inputs#I4 item 4).** Only after steps 12–15 are green on
    the fake (every block entry before the round) and the chunk's files are landed. The round as at step 10, its live
    entry labelled `S0R-2` with the same floor and `--spare 1`: the rig's ledger then admits `S0R-2` (no spare spent
    yet) and refuses `S0R-3` by its own rule, so the third start cannot be made tonight. Implement records the
    summary whole in `evidence/live-starts.md` beside S0R's. The readings and what each means:
    - **the floor held** → the cause was the rig's fresh config; `trust-record` reads `pass` or `fail`, and step 11's
      two ends apply (pass: the row verified on 2.1.325 in the rig's private home; fail: Run F's word and facts named,
      the founder's fork for the morning). Then the operator pass. F2 (the product finding) stands for the founder
      either way;
    - **still `none` on B–F with `seed-markers: written`** → the first-run config is NOT the cause; the step-13
      facts name what stood (which literal, on which row, the first family, the last column); implement STOPS before
      the operator pass, F1 is updated with those facts, and **`S0R-3` is NOT spent** — it is left for the founder;
    - **any other red** (a floor row below `pass` with B–F reading `box`) → its rows and facts recorded, implement
      STOPS before the operator pass, no spare spent, F1 updated;
    - **a start refused for the token window** — uncounted: implement stops and says so, and sets no timer.
    **As read (Revision 2):** the second end — still `none` on B–F with `seed-markers: written`; `S0R-3` not spent.

17. **The `VC` arm: the rig's own child at 80×24, read and stopped with no key — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`,
    `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`.**
    - `Arm::VC` (word `vc`): unwrapped (`wrapped` none), no viola home (`has_vhome` false), its cwd trusted
      (`trusted` true). `Arm::parse("vc")`; `Arm::of_label` takes `S0C` alone as `VC` (no spare label: `S0C-2` reads
      none).
    - In `start`, the `V` arm's seed steps run for `VC` too, in the same order: the git root (`git-root:`), the trust
      seed at the root's key, the six markers at the version read from the program by path (`seed-markers:`); a
      failed step refuses the start `seed`. `record-left` stays the `V` arm's (no verify writes a record here).
    - The pty: `run_child` spawns `VC` at `viola_pty::Size::DEFAULT` (80×24), every other arm at the rig's 210×45. The
      rig's `Model` gains a size (`Model::sized(rows, cols)`, `rows()` read at its own width; `Model::new()` stays
      45×210), and `Session::spawn` builds its model at the spec's size, so the settle predicates and the kept frame
      read the 80-column screen. The summary gains `pty: <cols>x<rows>` from the spec the child was spawned with.
    - `Session` counts the bytes it feeds and keeps its spawn instant.
    - `arm_vc`: `first_frame` (its settle, its kept `start` frame — the local frame under `target/live-rig/<run>/`,
      never committed), `record_reading` (`box`, `trust`, `selected`, `options`, `box-text`, `modal`), then
      `screen: <word>` — `SIGNATURES.first_screen` over the model's rows, verify's own classifier — and
      `facts: <row>`: the stamp's `first_facts` row shape built from what the session holds at that read (`bytes`,
      `alive` = no exit yet, `exit` null while alive, `rows`, `box_any`, `last_byte_ms` = the last byte's ms from the
      spawn or null, and `SIGNATURES.first_facts`' `literals` keyed by `BOX_LITERAL_IDS`, `rule_above_prompt`,
      `first_row`, `last_col`) printed through the existing `facts_line`, so the line reads in S0R-2's
      `facts-<x>` spelling and the same row means the same screen. `keys: none`.
    - The stop: `VC` takes `stop_no_key` as `IM` does (`stop: killed-no-key`); no byte is ever written to its pty.
    - `viola-live-rig`'s `live` verb gives `VC` the child arguments `--model haiku` (Run F's argv) and no viola.
    - Closed words, whole numbers and literal ids only in the summary and the ledger; no row text (security
      `decision/live-session-screens-kept-local`).

18. **Its cases — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`, `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`,
    `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs`.**
    - `rig_rehearsal_vc_reads_its_first_frame_at_80x24_and_stops_with_no_key`: the fake agent under `--screens` told
      the private config by `--trust-config {config}/.claude.json` (as the V rehearsal is); asserts exit 0,
      `pty: 80x24`, the fake's `size` receipt `{"cols":80,"rows":24}`, `git-root: written`, `seed-markers: written`,
      `box: up`, `modal: none`, `screen: box`, a `facts:` line holding `alive=yes` and the `lit= adj= first= col=`
      suffix (its oracle values copied from the first run, testing.md 2026-10-16), `keys: none`,
      `stop: killed-no-key`, no key receipted, and the teardown (`assert_torn_down`). Its bounds are the case's
      shared `--settle 6 --deadline 15`; the rig it spawns is the test's own child, waited to its exit (`run`).
    - `the_arm_words_and_labels_parse` gains `vc`, `S0C` → `VC` and `S0C-2` → none.
    - `a_sized_model_reads_its_rows_at_its_own_width` (rig `screen.rs` tests): a 24×80 model fed one 100-character
      line reads 24 rows, the first 80 characters wide and the second 20.

19. **Green and landed before the start.** Every entry of the block before the live round runs green in the tree
    (the fmt, clippy, unit and integration entries and the rest), then the one control below, then hygiene and the
    land, as at step 16.

20. **The naming start `S0C` (inputs#I8 items 1–7).** The install read by path, the rig's census, then the live
    entry `S0C` under its own ledger `evidence/name-start.ndjson` with `--cap 1 --spare 0`: the rig's ledger admits
    `S0C` once and refuses any second start or spare by its own rule; the R6 ledger `evidence/live-starts.ndjson` is
    not touched, so `S0R-3` stays unspent. The census again after.
    - **Reading it.** Implement records the summary whole in `evidence/live-starts.md` §S0C (closed words only). It
      reads the kept local frame (`target/live-rig/<run>/screens/001-start.txt`, never copied, quoted or committed)
      and writes ONLY closed words: the dialog's name, one of `terms-notice` · `login` · `model-notice` ·
      `update-notice` · `permission-mode-notice` · `other`; how many options it offers; which is selected (its
      ordinal); whether it names an action the account's owner must take (`yes` · `no`); whether a compiled literal
      of ours could match it (`yes` · `no`). No row text, no account detail, nothing of the founder's config. When the
      frame shows something of HIS to act on (terms to accept, a login), one closed sentence says so; the rig accepts
      nothing.
    - **Set beside S0R-2.** The `facts:` row is compared with S0R-2's `facts-b` and `facts-f` field by field
      (`bytes`, `rows`, `lit`, `adj`, `first`, `col`): the same row means the same screen.
    - **No dialog** (`box: up` at 80×24): that is a reading — the dialog is verify's own doing, not the config's; the
      row of facts recorded, and which of verify's differences is left named (the timing, the sequence). No second
      start.
    - **The predicate.** The live entry reads GREEN when the start ran whole and printed its reading: `modal:` and the
      `facts:` line present, `census: 0`, `credentials: removed`, `scratch: absent`, `user-config` not
      `changed-by-rig`, `keys: none`, `stop: killed-no-key`. It reads RED on a teardown word missing or wrong — then
      it is recorded as read. The 21-row floor does not apply.
    - **Then STOP before the operator pass**, either way: implement says what the dialog is and appends an update
      to F1 in `.andromeda/runs/2026-11-18T01-02-09Z-implement/founder-forks.md` naming the three roads, decided
      then: a mend that is the chunk's (the rig's seed or arm) → a further revision and `S0R-3` on the founder's
      word; a thing of the account's owner → his act first; nothing nameable → the wrap as it stands. No timer and
      no scheduled wake.

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — the reading lines, `rows:`, `failing:`, `git-root:` and the `S0R` labels (step 6); `seed-markers:`, the V-arm marker call, the extended facts line (steps 12, 14, 15); the `VC` arm, its seed, size, reading and no-key stop, the `S0C` label (steps 17, 18)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs` — the sized `Model` and its case (steps 17, 18)
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — the `live` verb's `--model haiku` for `VC` (step 17)
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the V rehearsal's added assertions (step 6); `seed-markers: written`, the facts suffix (step 15); the `vc` rehearsal (step 18)

The block runs the formatter and linter, the agent crate's unit suite (the classifier, the facts, the stamp merge), the
root bin's unit layer, the changed integration binaries by name (`cli_verify` is in it: verify's runs change,
verification-harness.md 2026-11-17; `contract_ledger_probes` and `cli_version_gate` read the stamps; `contract_lints`
pins the moved override's order; `rig_rehearsal` is the V arm's rehearsal), then the whole integration and E2E layers
(every stamped binary and the harness boot copy the new `measured`), then the live round for the naming start `S0C`
(Revision 2; S0R and S0R-2 spent and RED, not re-fired), after which implement STOPS before the operator pass (step
20); the operator entries stand for a later word. The release check is not run: no test-only feature, binary or fake-agent code changes (the rig and its ledger
are test-only and already refused by it). Every root test that waits keeps the shared 12 s `WITHIN` under the 20 s lint;
the verify-driven cases have no test-side bound, the `ci` 20 s kill being theirs (test-plan
`decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill`), and the `verify_window_` case its moved 80 s. Verify's output feeds the
harness boot, so the operator pass boots one session `screen-smoke`, reads its status and cleans it up (boot never
piped, verification-harness.md 2025-09-25 addition). No mutation run (inputs#I1 item 8).

- `fs-adjacent` — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs`: the `rule_above_prompt` reader made to read `false`;
  case `first_screen_facts_name_each_literal_its_row_and_the_first_family`, its `rule_above_prompt` row by the name
  nextest prints for it (`…::case_{n}_rule_above_prompt`, copied from the first run), fired on entry 3. With the guard
  gone that row reads no adjacency — measured at implement.
Those two held at the second stopped run (`evidence/control-2.txt`); Revision 2 adds ONE (inputs#I8 item 8: one
control at most), fired the same way with `--timeout 900` after steps 17–18 are green:

- `vc-nokey` — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`: the `VC` arm's stop switched from `stop_no_key` to `stop` (the
  Ctrl-C presses); case `rig_rehearsal_vc_reads_its_first_frame_at_80x24_and_stops_with_no_key`, fired on entry 5
  (its filter holds `binary(rig_rehearsal)`; it builds the workspace, so the clone holds the rig and the fake). With
  the guard gone the rig types `\x03` into the child's pty: the fake receipts a key and exits, the summary reads
  `stop: ctrl-c 1`, so the case's `stop: killed-no-key` and its no-key assertion fail — measured at implement.
Each control's id is at most 16 characters.

`S0C` read: the rig's own plain `claude` 2.1.325 at 80×24, same private config, markers, environment and Run F's

overseer's dialog and read at 2026-11-18T07:41:36Z (his option, verbatim label); the rest is the overseer's
technical word.

1. **The founder's answer — «Verify с записью экрана».** `S0R-3`, the LAST live verify of this chunk's cap, is
   spent on a live `viola verify` that, when it FAILS, writes the first settled screen of a failed interactive run
   through the EXISTING `--record` path with its scrub, into the rig's local folder, never committed. This is a
   boundary widening he ratified in these words: today `--record` writes screens only when every row passes; from
   this chunk it also writes, on a failed verify, the first settled screen of each interactive run that did not
   reach the box — scrubbed as `--record` scrubs, to the record dir, nothing else. The plan lists the row change as
   an Expected amendment for the wrap's answer card, citing these words. After this start the chunk's cap is
   EXHAUSTED: no further live start without a new word.
2. **Bound of the widening — keep it as narrow as the words.** Only under `--record`; only when the verify failed;
   only the FIRST settled screen of a run whose first-screen word is not `box` (and not `trust` on Run A, where the
   trust dialog is the design); through the same scrub and the same bounded writer the passing path uses, the file

data.head: ## Revision 3 — S0C reached the box; S0R-3, the last live verify, keeps a failed run's first screen

body:

17–19 built and green — the block read `entries 18 · green 7 · red 0` on its first firing, the control `vc-nokey`
holds (`evidence/control-3.txt`), scope `clean`, hygiene `clean` and the land (tx 2609) before the start. Step 20:
`S0C` ledgered 2026-11-18T06:32:18Z under `evidence/name-start.ndjson` and read GREEN by its predicate
(`evidence/round-063211Z.txt`, `evidence/live-starts.md` §S0C): `screen: box` at `settle-ms 1062`, `modal: none`,
`facts: bytes=1390 alive=yes exit=null rows=10 box=yes last=661 lit=footer-agents@23,footer-cycle@23,rule@20,prompt@21
adj=yes first=banner col=80` — the rig's own plain `claude` 2.1.325 at 80×24, under the same private config, markers,
environment and Run F's argv, met NO dialog. So the screen Runs B–F met is raised by something verify does. `S0R-3`
was not spent; the R6 ledger `evidence/live-starts.ndjson` holds `S0R` and `S0R-2` alone. S0R, S0R-2 and S0C keep
their recorded readings and are not re-fired.

**The word (inputs#I11 item 1, the founder's own answer «Verify с записью экрана», given in the overseer's dialog
and read 2026-11-18T07:41:36Z, relayed; the operator's word inputs#I10):** `S0R-3`, the LAST live verify of this
chunk's cap, is spent on a live `viola verify` that, when it FAILS, writes the first settled screen of a failed
interactive run through the existing `--record` path with its scrub, into the rig's local folder, never committed — a
boundary widening he ratified in these words: «today `--record` writes screens only when every row passes; from this
chunk it also writes, on a failed verify, the first settled screen of each interactive run that did not reach the box
— scrubbed as `--record` scrubs, to the record dir, nothing else». After this start the chunk's cap is EXHAUSTED: no
further live start without a new word.

**Its bound, as narrow as the words (inputs#I11 item 2):** only under `--record`; only when the verify failed (a row
below `pass`); only the FIRST settled screen of a run whose first-screen word is not `box`, and not Run A's `trust`
(the trust dialog is Run A's design); one file per such run, named by its letter; the same writer the passing path
uses, its file mode and its link rule the same; nothing of the user's config, no environment value. A verify without
`--record`, and a passing one, write nothing new.

**What the scrub does to a folder path the dialog prints (measured from the code):** `ledger::scrub`
(`crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs:1285`, `scrub_text` beside it) rewrites every spelling of the user's home to
`~` and the user name, as a whole word, to `<user>`; `ledger::screen_fault` (`:1452`) then refuses a kept row, or its
seam with a neighbour, that still holds the home, a `/home/`, `/Users/` or drive-letter path, the user word or an
email-shaped token, and a refusal refuses the WHOLE recording before any file is written (security
`decision/fixture-scrub-and-refusal`). Under the rig, verify's `HOME` is the real one (`rig/isolate.rs:23-31`), the
scratch is `/tmp/viola-rig-<uid>/<run>/` (`isolate::default_scratch_base`, `:34-38`), Runs B–E stand in
`<scratch>/cwd/.viola-verify-<pid><suffix>` and A and F in `/tmp/viola-verify-*`: a folder path the dialog prints
there is kept AS WRITTEN — a `/tmp/` path is none the check refuses, and it holds the uid's digits, never the name. A
path under the home is kept as `~/…`; one the dialog wraps so that the home prefix splits across two rows is caught at
the seam and the whole recording is refused (`unable: a recorded fixture is not clean: FirstScreen.<x>.json row <n>
seam home-path`), nothing written. Each of these is a unit case (step 23).

**Leaned, decisive:** the first-screen file keeps the run's settled rows WHOLE through that scrub and check, not cut
by `signature_rows` (`ledger.rs:1419`). The cut keeps only rows holding a compiled literal, and B–F's screen holds one
(S0R-2: `lit=rule@1`, no modal literal), so the cut would keep its rule row and nothing that names it — and the word
asks the screen named and «a folder it names» (inputs#I11 items 2, 4). This is the widening's substance: today a
screen's row text leaves verify only as signature-only fixtures (security `decision/verify-signature-only`,
`decision/verify-screen-read-against-literals`).

**The three differences S0C leaves, from the code, no start (inputs#I11 item 6) — what the kept screen shows if each
is the cause:**

- **The ORDER.** Before Run B, verify runs the print probe (rows 01–07 pass) and Run A, killed with no key at its
  trust dialog, both under the same private config (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` kept, `rig/isolate.rs:231`), so either may
  have written that config before B starts; S0C's config met no earlier start. If this is the cause, B, C, D and F keep
  one and the same dialog whatever their own folder (S0R-2's B and F facts already read alike), naming no folder of the
  run's own, or another start's (`temp`: Run A's or the probe's), or a session or state an earlier start left.

- **HOW the folder is trusted.** B–E are trusted only through the parent walk from `.viola-verify-<pid><suffix>` up to
  the seeded root; F only by the record verify writes for its fresh temp dir; S0C stood in the seeded key itself. If
  this is the cause, the screen is a folder-trust-family dialog whose confirm label is not `Yes, I trust this folder`,
  naming the run's own dir (`own-run-dir`) — or, on B–E, the seeded root (`parent`).

- **The terminal queries** — closed from the code: no difference. Neither verify's pty (`viola_pty::pump_with_paste`,
  `src/cmd/verify/typed/run.rs:143-155`, `crates/viola-pty/src/pump.rs:133-160`: the child's writer carries only the
  input reader's bytes and the pastes, and its output goes only to verify's vt100 sink) nor the rig's session (its
  writer takes only the Ctrl-C and the typed keys, `rig/mod.rs:535`, `:793`) answers a device-attributes,
  cursor-position or keyboard-protocol query; a vt100 model answers none itself. S0C reached the box with none answered, and the live home's verify passes through the same unanswering pump. Were it the
  cause, the kept screen would be a partial draw with no dialog frame, which S0R-2's facts (a framed 9–10-row screen,
  a rule on row 1, 80 columns) already argue against. It is no candidate; the kept screen says so either way.

- The plugin (D1) is already argued against: F takes no plugin and read as B did. A screen naming a plugin or a mode
  would say otherwise.

**What Revision 3 adds:** steps 21–26 below. Implement re-enters at **step 21**: steps 1–20 stand as built, the tree
carrying them uncommitted. The S0C live entry is spent and leaves the block; the block's live entry is `S0R-3`.

    - **Set beside S0R-2.** The `facts:` row is compared with S0R-2's `facts-b` and `facts-f` field by field

install by path; a spare only after a named cause whose mend is this chunk, landed through a plan revision.

Spent: **2 of 3** (S0R, then S0R-2 under Revision 1). Spares spent: **1** (S0R-2). S0R-3: **not spent** — left for
the founder (Revision 1, inputs#I4 item 4; the rig's ledger ran under `--spare 1`, which refuses it).

## S0R — RED

- Ledgered by the rig before the start: `2026-11-18T01:22:58Z` (`live-starts.ndjson`, its `start` line); summary

## The floor

## The candidate (plan step 11)

Runs B, C, D and F read alike: `none` · bytes 1167–1319 · alive, no exit · rows 9–10 · `box_any` yes ·
last byte 322–651 ms, all far before 8 500 (the screen was quiet ~8 s before the read). Run E started no child (no

the table's K3 row assumed `box_any` no. K1 and K3 both have the founder's mend, so the disposition is the same.

quoted or committed). Run E did not start (no resume target: Run B never reached its turn), so no file for E; Run A read
`trust` by design and writes none.

| run | name | options | selected | owner act | compiled literal matches | folder | plugin | mode |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| b | browser-tools-prompt | 2 | 1 | no | no | none | no | yes |
| c | browser-tools-prompt | 2 | 1 | no | no | none | no | yes |
| d | browser-tools-prompt | 2 | 1 | no | no | none | no | no |
| f | browser-tools-prompt | 2 | 1 | no | no | none | no | yes |

- **What it is:** one and the same modal on every kept run — the CLI's prompt that it detected a browser extension
  and asks whether the session may use the browser tools; the selector stands on the first option, the one that
  keeps them off. It is drawn in the CLI's own dialog frame (the rule on row 1, `first=rule col=80`), which is why
  `box_any` reads yes and no prompt row or footer stands. D's body differs only in its mode sentence (D runs in plan
  mode; B, C and F name the auto mode).
- **Owner act: no** — no terms, no login; it is a choice, not something only the account's owner can do. Its cause
  lies on the host (a browser extension the CLI detects), not in the account.
- **Compiled literal: no** — neither modal literal (the trust dialog, the imports dialog) nor any box literal names it,
  so verify reads `none` and pastes nothing, as designed.
- **What raises it, as far as the screen says:** it names no folder (`none`), no plugin, and a mode only in its body
  text. It is the same whatever the run's own folder — B in a subfolder of the seeded root, F in a fresh temp dir, D
  under plan mode, F with no plugin — and the rig's own plain child at 80×24 under the same config, environment and
  argv (S0C) never met it. **It selects the ORDER** of the three differences Revision 3 listed: what verify runs
  before B — the print probe and Run A, killed at its trust dialog — under the same private config. The trust path is
  not selected (the screen is no folder-trust-family dialog and names no folder). Which of the earlier starts arms the
  prompt (the print probe or Run A) is not measured by this start.
- No byte was typed into it: `keys: none`, verify killed each run with no key (`decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs`).

### Disposition

The floor broke and the cause is NAMED: a browser-tools modal the CLI raises at an interactive start after earlier
starts in the same private config, which no compiled literal of ours knows. Its mend (a new compiled modal literal,
which moves `run`'s pre-send gate too; or verify's sequence; or the rig's config) is not this run's to choose:
implement stops before the operator pass. The mend and any re-read wait on a new cap asked of the founder; no further
live start was made.

- Crate dependency direction is enforced by manifests: `viola-core` depends on no viola crate; `viola-pty` knows no agent; `viola-hyprland` is the one compositor seam (queries and dispatches only through its closed request set), sync and tokio-free, depending on `viola-core` alone among viola crates; only `viola-agent-claude` knows Claude payload shapes, including those of `claude agents --json` (except, test-only, the live rig in `viola-e2e`, which reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value, and seeds its private Claude config, and the fake agent and the rig, which read a config's trust record); among the product crates only `viola-mcp` enables tokio (`rt`), and `viola-channel` lists it optional behind its `tokio` feature (the `TokioClient`), which `viola-mcp` enables; the root bin holds the subcommand dispatch, the run pump and the wheel, all of which consume only normalised events.

The only crate that knows Claude Code (test-only exceptions: the live rig in `viola-e2e` reads the key names and the source word of its own captured UserPromptSubmit payload, never a value, and seeds its private Claude config; the fake agent and the rig read a config's trust record). It parses hook payloads tolerantly and maps each hook to a normalised kind. It maps dialog answers to decision bodies (S3 / S7 / S8) and applies the R8 `CLAUDE*` strip. It resolves the child program (`resolve_program`: a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`) and holds the Claude-specific half of the CLI version gate: the capability ledger rows (compiled) with their `viola verify` checks, `parse_version`, the stamp merge and `verified` verdict, and the fixture scrub. The gate's spawn is the root bin's `run::version_gate`; the stamps I/O is `viola_state::stamps`. It keeps the vt100 screen signatures (readiness gate), parses, in the pure `agents` module, a `claude agents --json` answer (`parse` into rows or a closed `AgentsFailure`, `oversize` · `malformed`; the read itself is the root bin's `run::agents`), and normalises `prompt-submitted` (removes the long-paste wrapper, then reverses tag escaping; classifies `origin` driver/human/harness). It also holds the resume shapes `viola revive` launches with (`viola verify`'s Run E is the second caller of `resume_args(id, false)`): `PROGRAM` (`claude`), `RESUME_FLAG`, `FORK_SESSION_FLAG`, `is_session_id` (36 characters, hyphens at offsets 8, 13, 18, 23, ASCII hex elsewhere) and `resume_args(id, fork)`; it is the one product home of the two flag literals. It also holds the pure `marketplace` module, `viola plugin install`'s three documents built by `serde_json` (`marketplace_files`; `NAME` the marketplace `viola`, `PLUGIN_REF` `viola@viola`; its `.mcp.json` registers the MCP server `viola`, no hooks). No adapter trait yet: a second agent arrives as a sibling `viola-agent-<name>` crate, at which point the adapter trait is extracted into `viola-core`.

| Screen model | vt100 0.16.2 | Pre-send readiness and modal detection on `run`'s feed thread, handed a copy of the pump's output after the human's write, the screen of `viola verify`'s six interactive probe runs, and the screen the test-only live rig (`viola-live-rig`, in `viola-e2e`) reads of its child. `run` never reads content; `Screen::rows()` is the only row-text exit, read by `verify` alone for its signature-only `--record` screen fixtures and the rig-only first-screen record of whole scrubbed rows |

**What breaks:** under the nextest `mutants` profile a root test is killed at 15 s (5 s × 3), 5 s above `CONFIRM_WINDOW_FALLBACK`; a harness test (`package(viola-e2e)`) at 30 s. A test that waits out a designed floor (verify's waits of the gate's 8.5 s maximum, about 43 s; the product's 10 s confirmation window or a send under a held paste hint, 8.7–9.9 s, within a few seconds of the kill under host load) passes under profile `ci` and can be killed there, and a mutation run then ends before any mutant is graded. The first matching override wins, so a class override listed after a broader filter that also matches the test never applies.
**How to avoid:** a test that waits out a designed floor carries `send_window_`, `send_under_the_paste_hint_` or `verify_window_` in its name (30 s, 30 s and 80 s under `mutants`), and the `verify_window_` override stands ahead of `package(viola-e2e)`; `tests/contract_lints.rs` pins that order. Size any other new root case against the 15 s kill, not CI's 20 s.
**Fix if broken:** measure the floor first; rename the test into its class. A kill line moves only for a floor that is by design, with a planted-hang control, both readings recorded.
